**SYNTHETIC DATA: this report was produced from FAKE data generated by make-fixtures.js. None of these numbers describe the real MIR system.**

# MIR export analysis

Generated 2026-10-01 from folder `fixtures`. No free text and no person-identifying column is shown or stored in this report.

Settings: usable text = at least 15 characters after trimming/removing accents and case, and not in the trivial list (`ok`, `fait`, `repare`, `reparé`, `réparé`, `n/a`, `na`, `voir bon`, `idem`, `a verifier`, `-`, `.`). Repeat window = 30 days. Both are constants at the top of analyze-export.js.

## 5. Repeat repairs

Definition used: the same vehicle (VECLEUNIK) and the same repair code (PCODEREP) appears on a DIFFERENT work order 1 to 30 days after a previous one (by TBONS.DATE). Each (vehicle, code, work order) counts once.

- Events (vehicle + code + work order): **4,282**
- Repeat events: **712** = **16.6%** overall
- Caution: the first 30 days of the export cannot see earlier work orders, so the real rate is probably slightly higher than shown.

## 6. Vector memory estimate (ESTIMATE ONLY)

Assumption: one record per work order (3,060) plus one per complaint line (4,485) = **7,545 records** in this export. Size of the vectors alone = records x dimensions x 4 bytes x overhead factor. This is an estimate, not a measurement: it ignores the text and other fields, and the overhead factors (1.0 and 1.5) are guesses to bracket the answer. Quota used for comparison: 5 GB of vector storage per partition on the Basic tier, up to 3 partitions (figure taken from the project brief, not re-checked by this tool). GB here = 1,073,741,824 bytes.

| Dimensions | Overhead factor | Estimated vector size | % of 1 partition (5 GB) | % of 3 partitions (15 GB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1536 | 1.0 | 0.043 GB | 0.9% | 0.3% |
| 1536 | 1.5 | 0.065 GB | 1.3% | 0.4% |
| 3072 | 1.0 | 0.086 GB | 1.7% | 0.6% |
| 3072 | 1.5 | 0.130 GB | 2.6% | 0.9% |

This export covers the period shown in section 1. A longer history needs a proportionally larger estimate (records scale with the number of years).
